instruction: List the flight status information for all flights leaving Los Angeles airports for Seattle tomorrow.

metadata.explanation: Task variation that changes the flight route from 'New York to Columbus OH' to 'Los Angeles to Seattle'. The task maintains the same structure as the original: agent navigates Delta.com to search for flight status updates for a specific route tomorrow. The evaluator uses existing functions (get_active_tab_html_parse, get_rule_relativeTime, check_direct_json_object) to verify the agent successfully searched for LAX→SEA flights with tomorrow's date. No custom functions needed as we reuse the original evaluator structure.
metadata.changes: Only modified: instruction (LAX→SEA route), expected airports (LAX, SEA). Kept same: config, evaluator structure, all getter/metric functions.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies all instruction requirements: departure airport (LAX), arrival airport (SEA), and date (tomorrow)
Getter logic is semantically correct: get_active_tab_html_parse extracts flight info from Delta's active tab using appropriate CSS class selectors
Data extraction uses class_multiObject_child to get direct text nodes from 'mach-flight-context-info__wrapper__info--separator', correctly extracting departure/arrival airports
Relative time conversion is correct: get_rule_relativeTime properly converts 'tomorrow' to absolute date with format '{DoW}, {Month} {Day0D}, {Year}' matching Delta's date display
Expected values are semantically accurate for LAX→SEA route as specified in the instruction
Metric logic is appropriate: check_direct_json_object performs direct JSON comparison which correctly verifies extracted values against expected values
Data flow is logically sound: getter extracts JSON → relative time getter converts tomorrow to absolute date → metric compares extracted vs expected
All data types are semantically compatible throughout the evaluation pipeline
